previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hypoxia and hypotension due to severe pneumonia and sepsis. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, required vasopressor support initially, and showed gradual improvement in oxygenation and mental status. Delirium developed in the ICU and was managed by medication optimization. Repeat imaging showed slight improvement in bilateral pneumonia, and she completed a 7-day antibiotic course. Her chronic conditions, including paraplegia, chronic pain, and hypothyroidism, were managed throughout. She was discharged home on 2L oxygen with stable vital signs and instructions for ongoing chest therapy and medication adherence.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old woman with a history of T2 paraplegia and recurrent 
pneumonias p/w hypoxia. Started on Levofloxacin 1 day prior to 
admission for community acquired pneumonia. Hospital course 
according to active problem list.  
.  
# Fever, hypoxia, productive cough: CXR demonstrated R perihilar 
and bibasilar opacities suggesting reoccurring pneumonia. 
Patient is at increased risk of developing pneumonia based on 
mechanical constraints and poor clearance. In the ED she had low 
blood pressure (SBP ___, HR 94), underwent central line 
placement and started on Vancomycin and Zosyn for CAP that 
failed to symptomatically improve with outpatient levofloxacin 
therapy. Patient was admitted to the MICU where her blood 
pressure responded to IVF and was consequently transferred to 
the general medicine floor. Her blood pressure remained stable 
and oxygen requirement decreased to baseline > 93% on RA/2 L NC 
on antibiotics. Legionella antigen was negative, blood culture 
demonstrated no growth and sputum culture grew oral flora with 
rare growth gram negative rods. As patient failed outpatient 
Levofloxacin she was transitioned from IV Vanc/Zosyn to po 
Augmentin and continued to be afebrile with stable BP. She was 
discharged on Augmentin 10 days total for community acquired 
pneumonia (last augmentin dose ___. Patient encouraged to 
use inspirex at home to prevent recurrent infections.  
.  
# Positive urine culture: Patient has history of recurrent UTI 
secondary to straight cath. Urine culture grew KLEBSIELLA, which 
is most likely secondary to colonized bladder (for sensitivity 
see results). Regardless of whether patient has urinary tract 
infection vs. colonized bladder - Klebseilla infection is 
covered by 3 days of Zosyn and as outpatient on Augmentin 
(Klebsiella culture sensitive to Unasyn) for pneumonia 
treatment.  
.  
# TW inversion in anterior leads, in otherwise asymptomatic 
patient: Unlikely ACS. No chest pain. Cardiac enzymes negative. 
Repeat EKGs no changes.  
.

most likely hemoconcentrated due to dehydration. Throughout 
admission at baseline ___.
